output.summary: KEP-6132 proposes a PreQueueingHint extension point in the kube-scheduler: a plugin can pre-filter which unschedulable pods a cluster event could make schedulable, so the scheduler does not run QueueingHints for every unschedulable pod. The KEP is currently implementable at stage alpha.
output.rationale: The motivating problem is a thundering herd of pods (e.g., thousands of DRA pods created with ResourceClaimTemplates at once) that all get re-evaluated on each claim event. A reviewer's scheduler_perf run showed throughput rising from about 297 to about 711 pods/s with the feature on, which the reviewer called worthwhile. Review raised open concerns: a second pod referencing a generated claim, PodGroup membership lookup, and whether the async ResourceClaim queue should be separate.
output.outcome_reason: The sources give the status as implementable, stage alpha, but also show the KEP was later marked tracked/no and had a release exception filed on 2026-07-23 with the release team evaluating it. The sources do not state the final outcome of that exception request.

alternatives.option: Periodic sweep of the unschedulable queue to rescue missed pods
alternatives.why_not: Reviewer noted it causes an unpredictable, potentially long delay for pods such as a second pod sharing a claim, and questioned whether the sweep is meant to go away.

alternatives.option: Maintain a pod informer index mapping ResourceClaims to referencing pods
alternatives.why_not: Described as more expensive, but the author adopted an informer-based approach in the KEP update on 2026-06-09 after the reviewer's patch showed it working.

alternatives.option: Ship the asynchronous ResourceClaim event queue together with PreQueueingHint
alternatives.why_not: Benchmarking showed no throughput benefit and about 18% less CPU for scheduling; the author said they were open to dropping it, and reviewers asked for it to have a separate feature gate.

evidence.quote: No throughput benefit from the async queue. Profiling shows ~18% reduction in CPU available for scheduling due to worker goroutine overhead.
I think both should have separate feature gates. Then one can be turned off without affecting the other. A single KEP seems sufficient.
This KEP has filed an exception, the release team is evaluating and will be added back to the milestone after a consensus.
We can't break such a usage and cause the second pod to not get scheduled.
